workload: Qwen3.5-0.8B, RTX 4060 Laptop SM89, vLLM 0.28.1, GPTQ Marlin W4A16 backbone, tied BF16 lm_head, six natural prompts, 128 generated tokens, batch/concurrency 1

metadata_repair.symptom: vLLM created full-attention fused QKV layers as unquantized and then failed while loading GPTQ g_idx tensors
metadata_repair.root_cause: modules_in_block_to_quantize listed linear_attn and MLP projections but omitted quantized self_attn q/k/v/o projections that are present in model.safetensors
metadata_repair.repair: add self_attn.q_proj, self_attn.k_proj, self_attn.v_proj, and self_attn.o_proj to quantization_config.modules_in_block_to_quantize

comparison_to_prior_low_power_fp8_stock.boundary: directional only: both runs are low-power screens but were not process-interleaved

rank_diagnostic.mode: eager diagnostic with full BF16 reference logits on every decoded token
rank_diagnostic.interpretation: top-128 recall is sufficient in the eager diagnostic; compiled/CUDA-graph execution semantics or numerical behavior, not shortlist capacity, is the unresolved quality failure

conclusions: Stock GPTQ-Marlin W4 is directionally about 1.12x faster than the prior low-power FP8 stock screen, but this is not a process-interleaved qualification and the 248320x1024 tied output head remains BF16.
Specializing the residual BF16 output head exposes a large 1.52x performance opportunity even on top of a W4 backbone, so using the same quantization does not make the stock runtime locally optimal.
The current specialized-head implementation fails the token-identity gate under compiled CUDA-graph execution and is therefore not a production winner despite its speed.
The next experiment must isolate compiled-no-CUDA-graph versus CUDA-graph behavior or add a certified fallback; increasing shortlist size further is unsupported by the rank evidence.
